theory Subtyping

Semantic subtyping

Inclusion subtyping in CTT, set and intersection types, negative type discrimination, and function variance laws.

Semantic subtyping, refinement types, and intersection types in CTT.

In NuPRL's computational type theory, subtyping is semantic containment: `A` is a subtype of `B` if every element of `A` is an element of `B` with the same computational equality:

> Subtype(A; B) == ∀x:A. x ∈ B

This theory formalizes: 1. Preorder properties of subtyping (reflexivity, transitivity) and equivalence `SubEq`. 2. Extremal types: bottom `Void` is a subtype of every type. 3. Set-theoretic intersection `Intersect(A; B) == {x:A | x ∈ B}` as a greatest lower bound. 4. Refinement / set subtyping (`{x:A | P x} ≤ A`) and monotonicity under implication. 5. Variance laws for type constructors: - Functions: contravariant in domain, covariant in codomain. - Products: covariant in both components. - Unions: covariant in both components. 6. Concrete subtyping hierarchy: `Positive ≤ Nat ≤ Int`.

16 theorems, 6 abstractions, checked by replaying their tactic scripts on the kernel. Hover any piece of syntax for its kind, surface form, and uniform term; open Tactics, Proof, or Analysis to go deeper.

examples/subtyping.nuprl

Original source file
-- | Semantic subtyping, refinement types, and intersection types in CTT.
--
-- In NuPRL's computational type theory, subtyping is semantic containment:
-- `A` is a subtype of `B` if every element of `A` is an element of `B` with
-- the same computational equality:
--
-- > Subtype(A; B) == ∀x:A. x ∈ B
--
-- This theory formalizes:
-- 1. Preorder properties of subtyping (reflexivity, transitivity) and equivalence `SubEq`.
-- 2. Extremal types: bottom `Void` is a subtype of every type.
-- 3. Set-theoretic intersection `Intersect(A; B) == {x:A | x ∈ B}` as a greatest lower bound.
-- 4. Refinement / set subtyping (`{x:A | P x} ≤ A`) and monotonicity under implication.
-- 5. Variance laws for type constructors:
--    - Functions: contravariant in domain, covariant in codomain.
--    - Products: covariant in both components.
--    - Unions: covariant in both components.
-- 6. Concrete subtyping hierarchy: `Positive ≤ Nat ≤ Int`.
theory Subtyping

comment book "Semantic subtyping, intersection types, refinement subtyping, and variance laws."

abs Subtype(A; B) == ∀x:A. x ∈ B
abs SubEq(A; B) == Subtype(A; B) ∧ Subtype(B; A)

abs Intersect(A; B) == {x:A | x ∈ B}
abs Nat == {x:Int | ¬(x < 0)}
abs Positive == {x:Int | 0 < x}

abs Bot == Void

soft Subtype, SubEq, Intersect, Nat, Positive, Bot

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Preorder properties of Subtype
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem subtype_refl :
  ∀A:U{i}. Subtype(A; A)
proof
  intro A
  intro x
  auto
qed

theorem subtype_trans :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. ∀C:U{i}.
    Subtype(A; B) → Subtype(B; C) → Subtype(A; C)
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro C
  intro hab
  intro hbc
  intro x
  elim 4 with x THENL [
    hyp,
    elim 5 with x THENL [hyp, hyp]
  ]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Subtyping equivalence: SubEq
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem subeq_refl :
  ∀A:U{i}. SubEq(A; A)
proof
  intro A
  split THENL [
    lemma subtype_refl [A] THEN hyp,
    lemma subtype_refl [A] THEN hyp
  ]
qed

theorem subeq_sym :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. SubEq(A; B) → SubEq(B; A)
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro h
  elim 3
  split THENL [hyp 5, hyp 4]
qed

theorem subeq_trans :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. ∀C:U{i}.
    SubEq(A; B) → SubEq(B; C) → SubEq(A; C)
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro C
  intro hab
  intro hbc
  elim 4
  elim 5
  split THENL [
    lemma subtype_trans [A, B, C] THEN elim 10 with u THENL [hyp, elim 11 with u1 THENL [hyp, hyp]],
    lemma subtype_trans [C, B, A] THEN elim 10 with v1 THENL [hyp, elim 11 with v THENL [hyp, hyp]]
  ]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Extremal types: Bot
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem subtype_bot :
  ∀A:U{i}. Subtype(Bot; A)
proof
  intro A
  intro x
  elim 2
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Refinement / Set subtyping
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem subtype_set :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀P:(A → U{i}). Subtype({x:A | P x}; A)
proof
  intro A
  intro P
  intro x
  hyp
qed

theorem subtype_set_eq :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀a:A. Subtype({x:A | x = a ∈ A}; A)
proof
  intro A
  intro a
  intro x
  hyp
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Set-theoretic intersection: greatest lower bound
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem subtype_intersect_l :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. Subtype(Intersect(A; B); A)
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro x
  hyp
qed

theorem subtype_intersect_r :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. Subtype(Intersect(A; B); B)
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro x
  elim 3
  hyp
qed

theorem subtype_intersect_glb :
  ∀A:U{i}. ∀B:U{i}. ∀C:U{i}.
    Subtype(C; A) → Subtype(C; B) → Subtype(C; Intersect(A; B))
proof
  intro A
  intro B
  intro C
  intro hca
  intro hcb
  intro x
  intro with x THENL [
    elim 4 with x THENL [hyp, hyp],
    elim 5 with x THENL [hyp, hyp]
  ]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Structural variance laws: Arrow, Product, Union
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Arrow: contravariant domain, covariant codomain
theorem subtype_arrow :
  ∀S1:U{i}. ∀S2:U{i}. ∀T1:U{i}. ∀T2:U{i}.
    Subtype(S2; S1) → Subtype(T1; T2) → Subtype(S1 → T1; S2 → T2)
proof
  intro S1
  intro S2
  intro T1
  intro T2
  intro hs
  intro ht
  intro f
  eq
  elim 5 with x THENL [
    hyp,
    elim 7 with x THENL [
      hyp,
      elim 6 with y1 THENL [hyp, hyp]
    ]
  ]
qed

-- Product: covariant in both components
theorem subtype_prod :
  ∀A1:U{i}. ∀A2:U{i}. ∀B1:U{i}. ∀B2:U{i}.
    Subtype(A1; A2) → Subtype(B1; B2) → Subtype(A1 × B1; A2 × B2)
proof
  intro A1
  intro A2
  intro B1
  intro B2
  intro ha
  intro hb
  intro p
  elim 7
  intro with u THENL [
    elim 5 with u THENL [hyp, hyp],
    elim 6 with v THENL [hyp, hyp]
  ]
qed

-- Union: covariant in both components
theorem subtype_union :
  ∀A1:U{i}. ∀A2:U{i}. ∀B1:U{i}. ∀B2:U{i}.
    Subtype(A1; A2) → Subtype(B1; B2) → Subtype(A1 ⊎ B1; A2 ⊎ B2)
proof
  intro A1
  intro A2
  intro B1
  intro B2
  intro ha
  intro hb
  intro u
  elim 7 THENL [
    intro left
    elim 5 with u1 THENL [hyp, hyp],
    intro right
    elim 6 with v THENL [hyp, hyp]
  ]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Concrete arithmetic subtyping hierarchy: Positive ≤ Nat ≤ Int
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem subtype_nat_int :
  Subtype(Nat; Int)
proof
  intro x
  hyp
qed

theorem subtype_pos_int :
  Subtype(Positive; Int)
proof
  intro x
  hyp
qed
